evidence: The as-grown WS2 is amorphous in nature and characterized in detail by XPS and Raman spectroscopic analysis. X-ray diffraction (XRD) measurements were executed with Bruker D8 Advanced diffraction... XPS survey of the film in the binding energy range of 0 –1000 eV showed the presence of different W and S electronic states. Raman spectroscopy was further performed with a 514.5 nm laser source to determine the Raman active vibrational modes in the as-grown material. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) study was carried out for ALD deposited WS2 not only to determine the surface species after each half reactions but also to observe the self-limiting growth of the film. Residual gas analyzer (RGA) was performed to know the possible by-products during the ALD of WS2. The self-limiting growth of the film is investigated using QCM and complimented by FTIR study.
